stem.text: Let f be the function defined by \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{- 2 x^{2} + x}{x}, & x \ne 0 \\ 0, & x = 0 \end{cases} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = 0 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is not continuous at \( x = 0 \), because the limit of f(x) there is 1 while f(0) = 0.

worked_solution.text: The function value at the boundary is \( f(0) = 0 \), from the second line of the rule.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the function at the input

worked_solution.text: For \( x \ne 0 \) the quotient simplifies to \( 1 - 2 x \), so \( \lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = 1 \) from both sides.
The limit exists and equals 1, but \( f(0) = 0 \), so the limit does not equal the function value and f is not continuous at \( x = 0 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: the limit must equal the function value

options.label: f is continuous at \( x = 0 \), because the limit of f(x) there is 0, which equals f(0).
options.derivation: the function value at the input reported as the limit, so the limit and the value appear to agree

options.label: f is continuous at \( x = 0 \), because the limits from the left and from the right are both 1.
options.derivation: continuity concluded from the agreement of the one sided limits, with the function value never compared

options.label: f is not continuous at \( x = 0 \), because the quotient gives 0/0 at \( x = 0 \), so f(0) is undefined.
options.derivation: x = 0 substituted into the quotient, which applies only for x not equal to 0, giving 0/0
